scenes.heading: Editing and proofreading
scenes.sub: Three minutes that win back easy marks
scenes.say: Everyone makes small slips when they write fast. A missing full stop. Their instead of there. Proofreading in the last few minutes wins those marks back. Here's how.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A chef tastes the dish before it leaves the kitchen
scenes.science: A writer checks the piece before handing it in
scenes.breaks: a chef can add salt in seconds; you should fix small errors, not rewrite whole paragraphs at the end.
scenes.say: Think of a chef tasting the dish before it goes out. A quick check catches what's missing. Proofreading is your taste test. But just like the chef, make small fixes. Don't start cooking a new dish.

scenes.heading: The three-minute check
scenes.say: Here's the three-minute check. First, read for sense: any missing or repeated words? Second, hunt for your usual errors. Third, check the edges: a capital at the start of every sentence and a full stop at the end.

scenes.heading: Errors to hunt
points: Comma splices: two sentences, one comma
scenes.say: Hunt for these. Comma splices, where two sentences are joined by just a comma. Fragments, with no main clause. Tense slips, like walked and then see. And sound-alikes: its and it's, their, there and they're. Expand it's to it is to test it.

scenes.heading: Fix the comma splice
scenes.question: The match was cancelled, it had rained all night.
lines: A comma alone can't join them
The match was cancelled because it had rained…
scenes.say: Fix this: the match was cancelled, it had rained all night. Both sides are full sentences, so a comma can't join them. The rain caused it, so use because: the match was cancelled because it had rained all night.

scenes.heading: TiPToP for paragraphs
scenes.say: When should you start a new paragraph? Remember TiPToP. A change of time, place, topic, or a new person speaking.

points: Edit as you write, proofread at the end
scenes.say: Quick recap. Edit as you write and proofread at the end. Check sense, then your top errors, then the edges. Expand contractions to test them. And use TiPToP for paragraphs. Now try the practice questions!
